title: Graph World Model
severity_scope: The RAG comparison is incompatible with the disclosed ordinary common-test accuracy interpretation. The released implementation has a separately assessed Minor defect. Alternative unreported aggregation protocols remain unresolved.

findings.title: Overall and difficulty-specific RAG accuracies imply incompatible test-set compositions
source_locations: Original PDF p.7, Section 5, RAG metric defined as accuracy
Original PDF p.8, Table 7 and Section 5.1
Original PDF pp.16–17, Appendix A.5, easy/hard categories and 8:1:1 split
findings.claim: Table 7 supports comparison on LongBench v2 and the stated superiority of the shared GWM with 2k context over long-context baselines, with GWM-E superior to GWM-T.

assumptions.basis: Section 5 explicitly calls the evaluation metric accuracy; no macro-averaging definition is supplied in inspected methods/appendix.
The disclosed 8:1:1 dataset split and cross-method Table 7 comparison; per-row alternative subsets or changing-split averages are not disclosed.

assumptions.condition: Easy and hard partition the test questions
assumptions.basis: Appendix A.5 describes the two difficulty levels and Table 7 reports them alongside overall results.

assumptions.condition: Rounding error at most 0.005 percentage points in each displayed number
assumptions.basis: Two decimal places; conservative necessary interval allows total residual 0.01.

evidence.method: Analytic partition identity plus independently authored exact rational arithmetic; original PDF Table 7 pixels actually viewed.
evidence.identity: For p=n_easy/(n_easy+n_hard), O_m=p*E_m+(1-p)*H_m for every method on a common test set.
evidence.conclusion: The intervals are disjoint; the published table cannot be reconciled under the disclosed common-test sample-accuracy interpretation. All seven rows were checked.

alternative_readings_and_counterevidence: Transcription errors could explain the table, but the check cannot identify which entries need correction.
Different test subsets can yield different implied difficulty fractions, but would change the cross-method comparison population.
Undisclosed macro-averaging with different weights for overall and stratum metrics can change the identity; an exact estimand is needed.

Averages over changing random splits can have composition/performance covariance and do not necessarily obey the fixed-split identity. No such repeated-split protocol was found in the inspected materials.
Repeated stochastic predictions on the same fixed test set preserve the identity after averaging and do not explain the discrepancy.
The arithmetic does not establish fabrication, identify the erroneous method, or establish that a corrected ranking reverses.
findings.core_dependency: The table directly supports a principal empirical claim of a shared graph-conditioned model outperforming specialized/long-context competitors. The contradiction materially compromises that reported evidence, without requiring failure of all tasks or a demonstrated benchmark reversal.

repair.description: Supply test IDs, difficulty labels, predictions, scoring and aggregation; recompute on the declared common population or substantiate a different estimand. The partition identity is a verified consistency check, not replacement experimental results.

findings.remaining_evidence: Exact cause, valid aggregation protocol, corrected entries and survival of the reported advantage remain Needs Evidence.

focused_check.method: Relevant frozen source passages/static source, existing actual check output and independent analytic integration; no author-code execution.
focused_check.conclusion: For a common fixed test partition, overall accuracy is p times easy plus (1-p) times hard. The checked rounding intervals for the printed rows have no common p, including disjoint BM25 and GWM-T intervals. Alternative undisclosed weighting or changing subsets remain explicit limitations. Major concerns internally inconsistent core RAG evidence, without a fabrication or ranking-reversal claim.

findings.title: Missing internal imports and an unconditional dataset-construction raise prevent using the released training path
findings.claim: The linked released code provides an implementation and training path for the described GWM.

assumptions.basis: Manifest commit 4b9fe29f7e8fb2e7a6162956d86f8eaeffc2516b, tree complete, 63 files and no exclusions.

assumptions.condition: Ordinary Python relative import and for-else semantics
assumptions.basis: Static package paths and AST nesting directly checked; author code was never executed.

evidence.imports: All three relative llaga_* modules imported by model/__init__.py are absent; the directory instead contains gwm_llama.py.
evidence.class_names: gwm_llama.py imports GWMMetaModel/GWMMetaForCausalLM but names undefined GWMMMetaModel and LlagaMetaForCausalLM bases.
evidence.control_flow: Dataset loop at line663 has a for-else whose first statement is unconditional raise ValueError at703. No break exists in the loop subtree. Normal loop completion raises; an iteration exception also prevents successful construction. Sample-population statements after the raise are unreachable in that block.
evidence.method: Source reads, existence checks, and AST parsing only.

alternative_readings_and_counterevidence: An unpublished working tree or different experimental commit could have been functional; no experiment-commit identity is established.
Acknowledged upstream LLaGA/LLaVA lineage explains names but does not resolve missing relative modules in this package.
Repairing only one import cannot certify a working implementation because additional class-name/control-flow defects remain.
findings.core_dependency: Supported harm is to released-artifact usability. No demonstrated dependency links these failing source bytes to the published numerical results, so this finding remains Minor and is not used to invalidate the method or scores.

repair.description: Requires an internally consistent package and a corrected, tested dataset constructor; no author source was edited or executed.

focused_check.method: Relevant frozen source passages/static source, existing actual check output and independent analytic integration; no author-code execution.
focused_check.conclusion: Pinned module paths and undefined class names were statically checked, as was the dataset loop's for-else raise with no break. These are concrete release usability defects. Historical experiment execution is not tied to this snapshot, so the report correctly retains Minor and does not claim an end-to-end repair.

no_issue_found_scope: Graph propagation and conditional decoding formulas are coherent at the stated architectural level.
The paper explicitly distinguishes zero-shot and subsequent few-shot tuning; Agent and RAG transfer results are not conflated in this review.
The disclosed ALFWorld BERTScore measures imitation text rather than an unreported rollout-success metric.
Other reported task scores were not empirically refuted.

focused_scope_check.result: The architecture's inspected algebra and reported non-RAG scores are not certified globally or refuted by the RAG identity failure. Qualitative-image quality, raw runs, exact historical commit and full preprocessing remain outside the demonstrated scope.
